questions.q: Yesterday I met my friend who is now a doctor and ___ musician. Find the error.
questions.explain: Rule: when two nouns describe the SAME person and are joined by 'and', the article comes only before the first noun. Here the friend is one person who is both doctor and musician, so the second 'a' is wrong. Correct sentence: '...is now a doctor and musician.' If they were two different people, both articles would stay.

options: Despite of several disputes, they stayed.
Despite of the fact they stayed.
questions.explain: 'Despite' is already a complete preposition and never takes 'of' — the error 'despite of' is a classic trap. Its cousin 'in spite' DOES need 'of' ('in spite of disputes'). 'Although' is a conjunction, so 'although of' is never correct.

'A number of' always takes a PLURAL noun — it means 'several'. Contrast with 'the number of', which takes a singular verb ('The number of cases IS rising'). Also, only the noun 'economies' fits; 'economical' is an adjective.

'Constant' = steady, unchanging. 'Fitful' = irregular, starting and stopping — the direct opposite. Watch out: 'perpetual' (never-ending) is a SYNONYM of constant, and 'prevalent' means widespread, which is unrelated.

questions.q: Spot the misspelt word: plosible / explanation / government
questions.explain: The word is PLAUSIBLE (p-l-a-u-s-i-b-l-e), meaning reasonable or believable. Remember it with 'applause': plau-sible. 'Explanation' and 'government' (note: govern + ment, no extra n) are spelt correctly.

'Fetching' means going somewhere and bringing something back — exactly what collecting water involves. 'Captivating' means fascinating people, 'abandoning' means leaving behind, 'conveying' means communicating ideas. Only fetching fits daily water collection.
'Neither of' is always singular — think of it as 'not one and not the other'. So it takes 'is', never 'are/were/have'. Same rule for 'either of' and 'each of': 'Each of the boys HAS a pen.'

questions.q: All pens are books. Some books are chairs. Valid conclusion?
options: Either 'some pens are chairs' or 'no pen is chair'
questions.explain: All + Some yields NO definite conclusion (the middle term 'books' isn't distributed to link pens to chairs). But 'Some pens are chairs' and 'No pen is a chair' are complementary (same subject-predicate, one Some one No) — one must be true. Hence either-or.

questions.q: 'Only a few Perk is Kitkat' implies?
options: Some are + some are not (both definite)
questions.explain: 'Only a few' is special: it guarantees BOTH 'Some Perk are Kitkat' AND 'Some Perk are NOT Kitkat' as definite conclusions. It behaves like Some + Some-not combined — a favourite trap because test-takers treat it as plain 'some'.
Each letter shifts +1: C→D, A→B, T→U. Apply to DOG: D→E, O→P, G→H = EPH. First check constant shifts (+1/+2) before trying complex patterns.

questions.q: 'She is my grandfather's only son's daughter.' She is?
questions.explain: Work inside-out: grandfather's only son = my father. Father's daughter = my sister (or self if the speaker is female — with 'she', it's sister). Inside-out decoding prevents the classic mistake of jumping to aunt.

questions.q: 8 around a circle facing centre. R's right side is?
questions.explain: Facing the centre, your right hand points anti-clockwise around the circle. Verify: stand at the top facing down (centre) — your right is the left side of the page = anti-clockwise direction. Facing AWAY from centre flips it.

questions.q: Govt bans plastic. Assumption 'plastic is harmful'?
questions.explain: An assumption must be unstated yet NECESSARY for the statement. A ban only makes sense if plastic is considered harmful → implicit. 'People will obey' is NOT implicit (compliance isn't required for the decision to ban). Test: negate it — if negation kills the statement, it's implicit.

questions.q: Facing south, turn left, then left again. Facing?
questions.explain: Facing south, your left is east: South→East. Turn left again from east: left of east is north. So North. Two lefts (or two rights) = U-turn to the opposite direction.

questions.q: 'He is the son of my grandmother's only son.' He is my?
questions.explain: Grandmother's only son = my father. Father's son = my brother. Note: if the speaker is male it's 'brother'; the phrasing points to a male relative of the same generation → brother.

questions.q: C top floor, A just below C, B just below A (5 floors). B's floor?
questions.explain: Stack from top: C=5th, A=4th (just below C), B=3rd (just below A). 'Just below/above' means immediately adjacent — the strongest, easiest clue; always place it first.

questions.q: Rs.4800 for 2y at 20% SI. Interest reinvested 2y at 10% CI. Interest from Y?
questions.explain: Step 1 — SI from X: 4800 × 20% × 2 = Rs.1920. Step 2 — this 1920 becomes principal for Y: amount = 1920 × 1.1 × 1.1 = Rs.2323.2. Step 3 — CI interest = amount − principal = 2323.2 − 1920 = Rs.403.2. Trap: 384 is 20% of 1920 (one year's interest), not two years compounded.
The extra 20 seconds (36−16) cover exactly the 600m platform, so speed = 600/20 = 30 m/s. Train length = 30×16 = 480m. Shortcut for these Qs: speed = platform length ÷ (platform time − pole time).
Each term is an odd cube plus 2: 1³+2=3, 3³+2=29, 5³+2=127, 7³+2=345, so 9³+2=729+2=731. Clue: numbers just above perfect cubes (127, 345) scream 'cube ± constant'.

Need two numbers multiplying to +135 with sum +24 (signs: −24m means both negative factors... actually both numbers are positive 15 and 9 since −15×−9=+135 and −15−9=−24). So m=15 or 9. Rule: for x²−Sx+P, find factor pairs of P summing to S.

questions.q: 144 km/h train crosses a pole in 12.5s. Length?
questions.explain: Convert km/h to m/s with ×5/18: 144×5/18 = 40 m/s. A pole means distance = train's own length = speed × time = 40×12.5 = 500m. Memorize ×5/18 (km/h→m/s) and ×18/5 (reverse).
Total = average × count = 50×10 = 500 kg. Nearly every average Q is solved by converting to totals first, operating, then converting back.
Each term doubles and adds 1: 5×2+1=11, 11×2+1=23, 23×2+1=47, so 47×2+1=95. Pattern family: ×2±1, ×3±2 — test these before anything exotic.

Need factors of 30 summing to 11: 5 and 6 (5×6=30, 5+6=11), both positive because the middle sign is negative... check: (x−5)(x−6)=x²−11x+30 ✓. So x=5 or 6. Option (b) multiplies to 30 but sums to 13 — always verify the sum.

questions.q: She ___ in hilly areas since her childhood.
questions.explain: 'Since + a starting point in the past' (her childhood) with an action continuing to now always needs the present perfect continuous: has/have + been + verb-ing. So 'has been living'. Simple present 'lives' only suits habits with no 'since' clause, e.g. 'She lives in Shimla.'

questions.q: The university will conduct exams after COVID-19 cases ___.
questions.explain: After time conjunctions (after, when, until, if, as soon as), use the PRESENT tense even when the main clause is future. The main clause already carries the future ('will conduct'), so 'will decline' repeats it wrongly. Correct: '...after cases decline.'

'Sustained' here means suffered/endured over time. 'Persisted' (continued to exist) is the closest match. 'Affiliated' means attached to an organisation, 'rendered' means provided/gave, and 'intermittent' (on-and-off) is nearly an antonym.

questions.q: Spot the misspelt word: observatory / residents / strom / alerted
questions.explain: 'strom' is missing its 'o' — the word is STORM (s-t-o-r-m). The others are correct: observatory (a building for watching the sky), residents (people living somewhere), alerted (warned).

'Reserve stock' is the standard collocation — a reserve is something stored for emergencies. 'Buffer stock' exists too (for smoothing supply), but in the phrase 'zero ___ stock' for emergencies, 'reserve' is the expected answer. Preserve/conserve are verbs (protect/save), not nouns for stored goods.

'Coherent' means logical, consistent and well-organised — what a policy framework must be. The other three all mean illogical in different ways: ludicrous (laughably absurd), spurious (false though seeming true), absurd (wildly unreasonable).

The fixed preposition with 'accused' is OF when naming the crime: 'accused of theft'. ('Accused for' or 'with' are common Indian-English errors.) Note the related pattern: 'charged WITH a crime' — accused→of, charged→with.

'Only A are B' REVERSES the All-statement: it means All B are A (every copy is a pen, but non-pens can never be copies). So 'all pens are copies' is false — pens need not be copies. Draw it: Copies circle fully inside Pens circle.

questions.q: A ≥ B > C = D. Is A > D?
questions.explain: Collapse the chain from A to D: A ≥ B (at least as big), B > C (strictly bigger), C = D (equal). ≥ combined with > gives strict >: A > D definitely. Rule: one strict link anywhere makes the whole chain strict; '=' links are neutral.
Opposite pairs sum to 27 (A=1+Z=26, B=2+Y=25...). M=13 needs 14=N. Shortcut: opposites are mirror positions — M (13th from start) ↔ N (13th from end).

questions.q: Facing north, turn 90° right then 180° left. Facing?
questions.explain: Track step by step: North →(90° right)→ East →(180° left)→ West. A 180° turn always lands exactly opposite, so from East you face West. Draw a small compass for multi-turn Qs.

questions.q: A, C, F, J, O, ? Next?
questions.explain: Gaps between letters grow: A→C (+2), C→F (+3), F→J (+4), J→O (+5), so next is +6: O+6=U. Arithmetic-gap series are the commonest alpha patterns — always compute gaps first.

questions.q: 40 students. Ravi 12th from left. From right?
questions.explain: Formula: rank from other side = total − given rank + 1 = 40−12+1 = 29. The +1 corrects double-counting Ravi himself. Check: 12+29−1=40 ✓.

questions.q: Walk 4m east, 3m north. Distance from start?
questions.explain: East and north legs form a right angle: distance = √(4²+3²) = √25 = 5m (the 3-4-5 triple). Never add legs (7m) — displacement is the straight line, computed by Pythagoras.

questions.q: A is B's brother, B is C's mother. A is C's?
questions.explain: B is C's mother, and A is B's brother → A is the mother's brother = maternal uncle. Chain method: replace B with 'C's mother' → 'A is (C's mother)'s brother' → uncle.

questions.q: Boxes X,Y,Z stacked. X above Y, Z below Y. Top?
questions.explain: Y is the middle reference: X is above it, Z below it → top-to-bottom order X, Y, Z. Top = X. Pick one item as anchor and hang every clue off it.

questions.q: Still:stream=6:1, upstream 20 km/h. Time for 126 km downstream?
questions.explain: Let still=6k, stream=k. Upstream = still − stream = 5k = 20 → k=4. So still=24, stream=4, downstream = 24+4 = 28 km/h. Time = 126/28 = 4.5 hours. Remember: upstream subtracts, downstream adds.
Alternate operations: ×48, then ÷6, repeating. 2×48=96, 96÷6=16, 16×48=768, 768÷6=128, so 128×48=6144. When a series jumps up-down-up, always test alternating patterns.
Simplify the right side first: 80% of 125 = 100, so RHS = 118−100 = 18. Then ? × 0.72 = 18 → ? = 18/0.72 = 25. Doing RHS first avoids messy decimals.
Cross-multiply first: (m−16)(m−12)=32 → m²−28m+192−32=0 → m²−28m+160=0. Factor: need pair multiplying to 160, summing to 28 → 20 and 8. Always clear fractions before factoring.
Side = perimeter/4 = 31. Area = 31² = 961. Memorize squares around 30: 29²=841, 30²=900, 31²=961, 32²=1024 — they recur constantly.

questions.q: 8% rent + 12% groceries, then 25% of the rest on transport. Total spent?
questions.explain: After rent+groceries, 80% remains. Transport = 25% OF that remainder = 0.25×80 = 20% of salary (not 25%!). Total = 8+12+20 = 40%. Trap: applying the second % to salary instead of the remainder.
Round to friendly numbers: ≈30% of 1000 = 300, plus ~1% of 1000 (=10) → 310. Approximation Qs reward rounding first, not exact computation.
First differences: +4, +6, +8, +10 — rising by 2 each time, so next difference is +12: 30+12=42. These are pronic numbers n(n+1): 1×2, 2×3, 3×4… 6×7=42.

questions.q: Rs.10000 at 10% CI for 2 years. Amount?
questions.explain: Amount = P(1+r)ⁿ = 10000×1.1² = 10000×1.21 = 12100. (Interest alone would be 2100 — read whether the Q asks amount or interest; here it's amount.)
New India Assurance — Mumbai HQ, founded 1919 by Dorabji Tata; India's largest public-sector general insurer. Contrast: LIC (life, 1956, Mumbai), GIC (reinsurance, 1972).
PM Fasal Bima: Kharif 2%, Rabi 1.5%, commercial/horticultural 5% — government pays the balance. Mnemonic: 2-1.5-5 (Kharif-Rabi-commercial).
Rs.5 lakh per family per year, cashless, for secondary + tertiary hospitalization — the world's largest health cover scheme, run by the National Health Authority. Launched 2018 from Ranchi.
GIC Re (General Insurance Corp, Mumbai) is the designated Indian reinsurer — it insures the insurers. LIC does life; AIC does crop (primary, not reinsurance); ECGC covers export credit.
Raised from 49% to 74% in 2021 to pull foreign capital into insurers. Timeline: 26 (2000) → 49 (2015) → 74 (2021).
Shishu ≤50k (infant enterprise), Kishore 50k–5L, Tarun 5L–10L (plus Tarun Plus to 20L now). Shishu=smallest, matching the name (shishu=baby).

Life Insurance Corporation of India came up in 1956 (Mumbai HQ) by nationalizing 245 insurers. Contrast GIC (general/reinsurance, 1972) to avoid the swap trap. 1938 is the old Insurance Act year - a deliberate distractor.

Gen 1 (1940s-50s, e.g. ENIAC/UNIVAC) ran on bulky, hot vacuum tubes. Then came transistors (G2), integrated circuits (G3), VLSI microprocessors (G4), and AI/parallel computing (G5). Order by shrinking size: tube → transistor → IC → chip.
Z = undo last action, Y (or Ctrl+Shift+Z) = redo it. Neighbourhood: X/C/V cut-copy-paste, S save, P print, F find, H replace, F7 spelling. These six shortcuts cover most CK shortcut Qs.
F5 starts the slideshow from slide 1; Shift+F5 starts from the CURRENT slide (handy while editing). F7 is spelling, F12 is Save As. Don't confuse with browser F5 (refresh).
HTTP=80, HTTPS=443, DNS=53, SMTP=25, FTP=21. Secure variants just add a port: the S in HTTPS buys TLS encryption and the padlock. Memorize this five-row table cold.

The CPU is exactly Arithmetic-Logic Unit (does the math) + Control Unit (directs traffic) plus registers. RAM/ROM/cache are MEMORY — a different subsystem. ALU+CU=CPU is the single most-asked architecture one-liner.
Magnetic Ink Character Recognition reads the special magnetic numbers at a cheque's bottom for fast clearing (the 9-digit MICR code). Barcodes are optical (supermarkets); fingerprints are biometric.
RAM is working memory — fast but VOLATILE (wiped on power-off). ROM is NON-volatile firmware (holds BIOS/boot code). That's why unsaved work dies in a power cut but the PC still boots.

The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India sits in Hyderabad (set up 1999). Trap options: RBI and SEBI are in Mumbai; PFRDA in Delhi. Regulator-HQ pairs are favourite static Qs.
Suraksha = ACCIDENT cover Rs.2L at ~Rs.20/year, age 18–70. Don't confuse with PMJJBY (LIFE cover Rs.2L at ~Rs.436, age 18–50). Pair them: Suraksha-20-accident vs Jeevan-436-life.

questions.q: DICGC cover per depositor per bank?
questions.explain: Deposit Insurance (RBI subsidiary) covers Rs.5 lakh per depositor per bank — raised from Rs.1L in 2020 after the PMC crisis. Covers all commercial + cooperative banks.
Compulsory under the Motor Vehicles Act: every vehicle must cover third-party injury/damage. It never covers your OWN damage — that needs a comprehensive/own-damage add-on.
IRDAI's trio: Bima SUGAM = online marketplace (compare/buy like Amazon), Bima VISTAR = rural bundled product, Bima VAHAK = women-led distribution force. Part of 'Insurance for all by 2047'.
74.04% literacy, sex ratio 943, density 382, population 121 crore. Cluster to memorize: 121cr–74%–943–382. (Next census delayed — check current affairs.)
Weight each bit right-to-left as 1,2,4,8: 1×8 + 0×4 + 1×2 + 1×1 = 8+0+2+1 = 11. Always expand positional values instead of guessing.
$ locks: $A$1 locks both (absolute — never shifts when copied), A$1 locks only the row, $A1 only the column, A1 fully relative. Test: dragging $A$1 down keeps pointing at A1.
SMTP (port 587/25) SENDS mail out; POP3 (110) or IMAP (143) RECEIVE it. Memory hook: S=Send. IMAP syncs across devices; POP3 downloads then usually deletes from server.

A virus attaches to a host file and needs you to run it; a worm is standalone and crawls networks by itself (e.g. WannaCry). Trojan = disguised as legit software; ransomware encrypts for money; spyware steals silently.
Memory uses binary: 1 KB=1024 B, 1 MB=1024 KB, 1 GB=1024 MB (2^10 each step). Telecom/storage marketing sometimes uses 1000, but exams expect 1024. 1024 KB would be just 1 MB.
UPI (by NPCI) = instant mobile payments via VPA. IFSC = 11-character branch identifier (4 bank code + 0 + 6 branch) used in NEFT/RTGS/IMPS transfers. One moves money, one addresses the branch.

questions.q: Which is NOT an OS function?
questions.explain: The OS manages hardware resources: processes (scheduling), memory, files, devices, security. Word processing is an APPLICATION running on top (like MS Word on Windows). Test: if users install it separately, it's not the OS.

Shortest Job First always picks the quickest pending job, minimizing average wait (provably optimal for known burst times). FCFS suffers the convoy effect (long job blocks all); Round Robin is fair but slower on average. Preemptive SJF = SRTF.

Normal forms nest strictly: 1NF ⊂ 2NF ⊂ 3NF ⊂ BCNF. Every BCNF table is automatically in 3NF (every determinant is a superkey), but a 3NF table can still violate BCNF. Stronger form ⇒ all weaker ones hold.
WHERE filters individual ROWS before grouping (can't use aggregates); HAVING filters GROUPS after GROUP BY (works with COUNT/SUM/AVG). Example: WHERE year=2024 ... GROUP BY branch HAVING COUNT(*)>5.

questions.q: Reliable claim upload: TCP or UDP?
questions.explain: TCP is connection-oriented: sequence numbers, ACKs, retransmission and ordering guarantee every byte arrives — exactly what document uploads need. UDP skips all that for speed (live video, DNS, gaming) and may lose data. Reliability ⇒ TCP.

AES (symmetric, one shared key) is ~1000× faster — used for the actual data. RSA (asymmetric, key pair) only exchanges keys and signs. SHA-256/MD5 are HASHES (one-way fingerprints), not encryption at all. Real systems are hybrid: RSA handshake, AES session (that's HTTPS).
